message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data. For the most up‑to‑date information on Los Angeles you can check one of the following:

| Source | How to use |
|--------|------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code, and view the AQI (Air Quality Index) and pollutant breakdown. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”, and see the live AQI, forecast, and historical trends. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Many local outlets publish daily air‑quality updates, especially during smog events. |
| **Mobile apps** (e.g., AirVisual, Plume Labs) | Install an app that pulls data from official monitoring stations and provides alerts. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, you can also use a voice assistant (Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa) and ask, “What’s the air quality in Los Angeles?” They typically pull from the same public APIs.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the AQI values or understanding what pollutants are most concerning!
